stem: Bellhaven Labs re-runs the same automation weekly, but changes made by hand in the console during the week are never detected before the next run overwrites them silently. They want a tool that specifically compares real infrastructure against the desired configuration before making any change. Which mechanism gives them that?

choices.text: A cron job that re-applies the same script every week regardless of what changed after the previous run.
A monitoring dashboard that alerts an engineer by email when a resource's configuration changes.
A backup snapshot of the environment taken before each weekly run, in case the run needs to be undone.
A tracked state record the tool consults before planning, so it can compare current resources with the configuration they are supposed to match, and show only the actual differences.

rationale: The key describes state-backed comparison: Terraform consults its tracked state before a plan, so it can compare real infrastructure against the configuration and show only the real differences, which is exactly the missing comparison step. A cron job that blindly reapplies the same script is the failure already described in the stem, not a fix. An email alert is purely observational and does not feed into any tool's own decision about what to change. A backup snapshot supports rollback, not detection of what actually changed before applying.
